name: GitHub CLI 2.105.0
body:
## What's Changed

## Subscribe to GitHub Event Streams with `gh event` (preview)

The new `gh event` command set lets agents, integrations, and scripts wait for pull request changes instead of polling GitHub:

```shell
# Wait for a review event
gh event listen --resource https://github.com/OWNER/REPO/pull/NUMBER --event com.github.pull_request.review.submitted.v1 --timeout 30m

# Wait for a check suite completion event
gh event listen --resource https://github.com/OWNER/REPO/pull/NUMBER --event com.github.pull_request.check_suite.status.changed.v1 --jq .data.conclusion

# List active event subscriptions
gh event subscription list
```

By default, `gh event listen` exits after the first event. Use `--count` to wait for several events or `--follow` to keep listening. Events are printed as CloudEvent JSON objects, with `data.api_url` pointing to the resource that changed.

Supported events include submitted reviews, pull request state and head changes, merge conflicts, and completed check suites. The `subscription create`, `list`, `view`, and `delete` commands manage subscriptions directly.

> [!NOTE]
> GitHub Event Streams is in preview. [Join the wait list](https://gh.io/event-streams-signup), read the [announcement](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-17-github-event-streams-is-now-in-preview), or see the [Event Streams documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/integrations/how-tos/using-github-event-streams).

## Protect private forks when deleting repositories

`gh repo delete` now warns when deleting a private or internal repository will also delete its forks. The additional confirmation is required even with `--yes`.

Non-interactive workflows and agents must explicitly accept the cascading deletion:

```shell
gh repo delete OWNER/REPO --yes --accept-cascading-deletion-of-private-forks
```

name: GitHub CLI 2.103.0
body:
## Expiring, auto-refreshing OAuth tokens (preview)

`gh` can now sign in with expiring OAuth credentials that it refreshes automatically. When you opt in, `gh` stores a short-lived access token alongside a rotating refresh token and refreshes the access token whenever it is needed, so you stay signed in without having to authenticate again.

To opt in for a single sign-in, run:

```shell
gh auth login --expiring
```

To prefer expiring credentials for every sign-in, run:

```shell
gh config set expiring_credentials enabled
```

`gh auth status` shows whether a credential is refreshable and when the current access token expires. Both `gh auth status` and `gh auth token` automatically refresh the access token when needed. Expiring tokens are available on github.com and GHE.com; on hosts that do not issue them, `gh` falls back to a regular non-expiring token.

If you use HTTPS as your git protocol, we advise using git 2.46 or newer and letting `gh` act as your git credential helper by running `gh auth setup-git`. This way `gh` serves and refreshes the expiring credential for git, and git does not cache it past its lifetime.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Expiring access tokens should not be cached. Scripts and extensions that store the output of `gh auth token` will eventually hold an expired token, so run `gh auth token` again each time a token is needed. Tokens supplied through `GH_TOKEN` or `GITHUB_TOKEN` are never refreshed.

For more information, see [Authenticating with GitHub CLI](https://docs.github.com/github-cli/github-cli/authenticating-with-github-cli#using-expiring-refreshable-tokens).

## Manage issue artifacts with `gh issue artifact` (private preview)

`gh issue artifact` brings issue artifacts to the command line. Users and organizations enrolled in the private preview can use the `list`, `view`, `create`, `edit`, `download`, and `delete` commands to manage issue artifacts.

```shell
# Create a Markdown document with an attached image
gh issue artifact create 142 signin-plan.md --attach ./signin-flow.png

# Create an HTML document
gh issue artifact create 142 menu-prototype.html

# List or view artifacts
gh issue artifact list 142
gh issue artifact view 142 2

# Update a document or restore an earlier version
gh issue artifact edit 142 2 --body-file signin-plan-v2.md
gh issue artifact edit 142 2 --restore-version 5
```

Artifacts can also be addressed by their GitHub URLs, and Markdown documents support image and video attachments with `--attach`.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Issue artifacts are in private preview. These commands only work for repositories enrolled in the preview. See the [Issue Artifacts private preview announcement and feedback discussion](https://github.com/orgs/community/discussions/205881) for access instructions and to share feedback.

name: GitHub CLI 2.102.0
body:
## Security

Four security vulnerabilities have been identified, and fixed, in this release. Users are advised to update gh to version `v2.102.0` as soon as possible.

`gh release download`, `gh run download`, `gh repo read-file --output`, and `gh attestation download` could write remote content to an unintended local file when the destination contained symbolic links.

See https://github.com/cli/cli/security/advisories/GHSA-39wj-f2f4-978v for more information.

`gh attestation verify` compared the `--source-ref` value case-insensitively, so an attestation built from a branch whose name differs only in case could satisfy a policy that named a different branch.

See https://github.com/cli/cli/security/advisories/GHSA-4mq3-hpgx-9cx8 for more information.

Interactive `gh skill search` passed repository paths from search results to `gh skill install` without an option separator, so a search result could inject installer options and change where skill files were written.

See https://github.com/cli/cli/security/advisories/GHSA-qcwj-mr2r-2cx7 for more information.

`gh attestation verify` matched the `--signer-workflow` value against only the start of the signing certificate's identity, so an attestation signed by a different workflow in the pinned repository could pass verification when its path began with the pinned value.

See https://github.com/cli/cli/security/advisories/GHSA-wjmr-j3rp-mh2g for more information.

## What's Changed

### 🐛 Fixes

* Allow `ghu_` tokens for supported actors to attach files by @BagToad in [#14516](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14516)
* Allow repo set-default --unset without an argument by @williammartin in [#14540](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14540)

### 📚 Docs & Chores

* Prioritize HackerOne for vulnerability reports by @BagToad in [#14497](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14497)
* Clarify reviewer-facing PR guidance by @williammartin in [#14509](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14509)
* Add a skill for chaptered CLI recordings by @BagToad in [#14475](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14475)
* Improve CLI recording rendering by @williammartin in [#14507](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14507)
* Mention gh CLI in the README intro by @BagToad in [#14517](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14517)
* Document search operator support in `gh search` help by @waldyrious in [#14519](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14519)
* Remove host versions from `gh project item-list` help by @BagToad in [#14553](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14553)

### :dependabot: Dependencies

* chore(deps): bump the codeql-actions group with 3 updates by @dependabot in [#14486](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14486)
* chore(deps): bump nodeselector/setup-apple-codesign from 0.0.2 to 0.0.3 by @dependabot in [#14487](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14487)

## Linux package repository signing key rotation

GitHub CLI's APT and RPM repositories, along with individual RPM packages, are now signed only with the new PGP key (fingerprint: `7F38BBB59D064DBCB3D84D725612B36462313325`)

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Linux users who installed `gh` from the official APT or RPM repositories before April 8, 2026, and have not refreshed their keyring, may now see package installation or update failures. Follow the [PGP signing key rotation guidance](https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/13118) to check and update your keyring. Users on Windows or macOS, and users who installed `gh` through Homebrew, GitHub Releases, another package manager, or from source, are not affected.

## Copy authentication codes to the clipboard by default

`gh auth login` and `gh auth refresh` now copy OAuth device codes to the clipboard by default, saving a manual copy step during authentication.

To persistently opt out, run:

```shell
gh config set clipboard disabled
```

Explicit clipboard options still take precedence for an individual invocation.

name: GitHub CLI 2.100.0
body:
## Experimental: Route GitHub API traffic through a custom host

Organizations can now route a GitHub host's API traffic through a gateway using the new per-host `api_host` configuration:

```shell
# Route API traffic for github.com through a gateway
gh config set api_host gh-gateway.example.com --host github.com

# Read the configured API host
gh config get api_host --host github.com
```

The original host remains in use for authentication, Git remotes, and browser URLs.

> [!NOTE]
> `api_host` is experimental and is not a security boundary. Requests may still reach the original host.

## What's Changed

### ✨ Features

* Honor per-host `api_host` routing across GitHub API requests by @williammartin in [#14104](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14104)
* Expose `api_host` through `gh config get` and `gh config set` by @williammartin in [#14332](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14332)
* Add `webhook` as an official extension by @williammartin in [#14326](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14326)
* Print full command help after command misuse when `gh` is invoked by a coding agent by @niik in [#14198](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14198)

### 🐛 Fixes

* fix(api): disable telemetry for unauthenticated GHES requests using absolute hostnames by @williammartin in [#14337](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14337)

### 📚 Docs & Chores
